findings.problem: Having correctly observed that the words of M.G.L. c. 112, s. 24B1/2(c)(5) ('administration of vaccines or the modification of dosages of medications prescribed by the supervising physician for asthma, ... osteoporosis and co-morbidities ...') do not state whether the disease list reaches the vaccine limb, the section then calls 'vaccinate under the agreement only as the agreement authorizes, for a referred and consenting patient 18 years of age or older' the course 'safe on every reading', and the second comparison table answers 'Yes' to a vaccine for any referred, consenting adult under a vaccine-authorizing agreement. On the reading the section itself leaves open (the list modifies vaccines too), a vaccine unrelated to a listed condition would fall outside clause (5), so that course is not safe on every reading.
findings.rationale: The section's method elsewhere (orientation[7]) is to identify the narrower wording and call only that safe on either reading; here it drops the narrower reading it has just raised. 247 CMR 16.03(5)(b) and 243 CMR 2.12(4)(e)2. do authorize vaccine administration as the agreement authorizes with no disease list, so a candidate following the regulations would not be misled on the regulatory rule, which is why this is Low. The fix is a wording change: either drop 'on every reading' / qualify the 'Yes' as resting on the regulations' separate vaccine item, or add that on the narrower statutory reading the vaccine should relate to a listed condition the agreement references.

results.summary: Verified against the current official texts of M.G.L. c. 112, ss. 24B1/2 and 24B3/4 (malegislature.gov), St. 2008, c. 528, s. 3 (enacted clause (5) identical to current text; approved January 15, 2009), 247 CMR 16.03(5) and 16.04(1), 243 CMR 2.12(1) and 2.12(4)(e)1.-8., and 105 CMR 700.003(F)-(G). Every quotation and paraphrase checked is accurate: the 18-year floor; the 30-day extension versus the regulations' two 30-day periods or longer specific authorization; modification versus initiate/modify/discontinue; the statute's patient-specific co-morbidities versus the regulations' co-morbidities confined to the eight conditions; the disease-state reference, referral, notice and consent sentences; the community pharmacy written referral/consent items, 16.04(1)(a)-(b), the 243 CMR 2.12(4)(e)4. consent-form statement, and the record duties with the 24-hour consent copy running from physician to pharmacist and copies to the patient 'in a timely manner'; the s. 24B1/2(d) Health Facility exemption confined to the business; the Schedule II-V bar in both the statute (agreement) and regulations (pharmacist); the three Schedule VI sentences; and 105 CMR 700.003(G)(4) Schedule VI only in a retail setting. The section does not claim that either the statute or the regulations control where they differ; it accurately reports s. 24B3/4 and offers the narrower wording as the safe course. Cross-references to the foundations, agreement, prescribing (including the regulations' separate 24-hour copy duty in 16.03(5)(e)2.) and Schedule VI sections are boundaries, not duplications or contradictions, as far as can be judged from this package. All four practice questions (MA-Q-0082 D, MA-Q-0083 C, MA-Q-0084 A, MA-Q-0344 A) are answerable from and consistent with the section, including their explanations. One Low defect: the vaccine discussion calls a course 'safe on every reading' that is not safe on the narrower reading of clause (5) the section itself raises, and the decision table answers 'Yes' on that basis. MINOR_EDIT for that wording only.
